title: Bajaj Finance Launches Rs 11,700 Crore QIP at Rs 992.25 Floor Price
excerpt: The institutional share sale is half of a Rs 17,500 crore capital plan, alongside Rs 5,800 crore of warrants allotted to promoter Bajaj Finserv at Rs 1,010 each.
body:
• Bajaj Finance launched a qualified institutional placement on Wednesday, November 11, to raise up to Rs 11,700 crore (about $1.25 billion), with a floor price of Rs 992.25 per share, Reuters reported.
  • The indicative issue price was Rs 1,025 per share, about a 5% discount to the last NSE closing price and above the SEBI floor price, according to the Hindu BusinessLine.
  • The QIP is one half of a Rs 17,500 crore capital plan: promoter Bajaj Finserv was allotted Rs 5,800 crore of convertible warrants at Rs 1,010 each on November 10.
  • The board approved the plan on October 1, 2026, and shareholders approved it at an extraordinary general meeting on November 2.

Bajaj Finance, India's largest private-sector non-banking financial company, has launched a share sale to institutional investors to raise up to Rs 11,700 crore (about $1.25 billion), setting a floor price of Rs 992.25 per share, according to Reuters reporting carried by the Hindu BusinessLine. The non-bank lender had approved the qualified institutional placement (QIP) in October.

The indicative issue price is Rs 1,025 per share — about a 5% discount to the last closing price on the National Stock Exchange, and above the Securities and Exchange Board of India's floor price of Rs 992.25, the BusinessLine reported. A QIP is sold only to qualified institutional buyers, with pricing set under SEBI rules; the final price and the number of shares issued depend on demand in the book.

The wider Rs 17,500 crore plan

The QIP is the second leg of a two-part capital raise. On November 10, Bajaj Finance allotted 5.74 crore convertible warrants to its promoter, Bajaj Finserv, at Rs 1,010 per warrant — about Rs 5,800 crore — with each warrant convertible into one equity share within 18 months, according to the warrant terms reported by Univest. Together the two legs total up to Rs 17,500 crore. The board approved the plan on October 1, 2026, and shareholders approved both legs at an extraordinary general meeting on November 2.

Why the company is raising

Bajaj Finance said the funds are for expansion, against strong credit demand. The balance sheet it is funding is large and still growing: the company reported consolidated profit after tax of Rs 6,367 crore for the September 2026 quarter and assets under management of Rs 5.85 trillion, and first-half profit up 28% to Rs 12,447 crore, according to company results summarised in market coverage of the raise.

What to watch

For investors — including the large diaspora holder base in Indian financial stocks — the QIP's final pricing and the identity of the institutional book will show how much appetite exists for Indian consumer credit at current valuations. The stock had risen about 13% over the past month into the launch. Kotak Mahindra Capital, Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, IIFL Capital Services and JM Financial were named as managers for the transaction in market reports.
nri_angle: Bajaj Finance is a widely held Indian financial stock among diaspora investors; the QIP pricing will signal institutional appetite for Indian consumer credit.
